rows.source: Schmidt & Schumann 1989, J. Fluid Mech. 200:511-562, doi:10.1017/S0022112089000753, §3.5 and Fig. 18 (p.540, 543); PDF https://elib.dlr.de/53323/1/Schmidt_Schumann.pdf (open access, text layer read)
rows.note: Text: updraughts and downdraughts 'correlated with strong horizontal velocities (up to 0.36 w*) in the surface layer'; Fig. 18a(i) caption: extremes of conditionally averaged u for updraughts -0.36 and +0.33 w* (antisymmetric about axis => |u| 0.33-0.36). Height of the peak not stated beyond 'surface layer'; the 0.36 is the extremum over the whole x-z plane (may also be the top outflow, see outflow row). Peak is for the updraught composite whose central w is 2.0 w* (zc=0.5 zi sampling): a strong-event composite, not an average thermal. Coarse grid (50 m) under-resolves the lowest 0.1 zi. LES: 160x160x48, dx=zi/32 (~50 m), zi=1600 m, w*=1.46 m/s, dry, zero mean wind, z0=1e-4 zi; conditional averaging over w-events at reference height zc=0.5 zi (local w maxima > rms w, min separation ~1.0 zi), 6<t*<7, ~16 updraughts/domain.

rows.note: Not separated: text says horizontal motions are strong 'near the surface and near the inversion' and Fig. 18 u extremes are only +/-0.33-0.36 w* over the whole plane, so top outflow <= ~0.36 w* (upper bound, value at z=0.8-1.0 zi not given). Needs reading the contour plot, not done (contour levels in caption increment 0.05 w*). No other source found.

rows.source: Schmidt & Schumann 1989, J. Fluid Mech. 200:511-562, doi:10.1017/S0022112089000753, §3.5 and Fig. 18 (p.540, 543); PDF https://elib.dlr.de/53323/1/Schmidt_Schumann.pdf (open access, text layer read)
rows.note: Fig. 18a(ii) caption: conditionally averaged updraught w field has min -0.1 w* (max 2.0 w*) = surrounding sink in the composite at zc=0.5 zi; composite averaging smears the ring (instantaneous ring is deeper). -0.96 w* is the centre of the downdraught composite (separate events, radius 0.5 zi), the other end of the range, not the ring. Text also: radius of updraught 0.33 zi, ratio updraught/downdraught speed 2.1 (cf. 1.5 Greenhut & Khalsa 1987). Instantaneous section (Fig. 13-14) shows a ring of downward motion at the inversion around penetrating thermals, no number.

rows.source: Schmidt & Schumann 1989, J. Fluid Mech. 200:511-562, doi:10.1017/S0022112089000753, §3.5 and Fig. 18 (p.540, 543); PDF https://elib.dlr.de/53323/1/Schmidt_Schumann.pdf (open access, text layer read); Lenschow & Stephens 1980 (via thermals.md)
rows.note: No LES/measurement number for the speed of the thermal as an object (Lagrangian tracking in dry CBL) found in open text. Only qualitative: Schmidt & Schumann §3.3 'bubbles are rising more quickly than the average updraught'. Brackets for the AIR speed, not the object: 0.45 w* mean in updraughts (L&S 1980), 2.0 w* peak of composite (S&S 1989). Lecoanet & Jeevanjee 2019 (arXiv:1804.09326, DNS, neutral environment) and Hernandez-Deckers & Sherwood 2016/Romps & Charn 2015 (cloudy) give no CBL w* normalisation.
